key_insight: Transformer-based quantum circuit synthesis works well when approximate outputs can be repaired, but exact discrete synthesis suffers from autoregressive drift as circuits get longer.
engineering_relevance: For fault-tolerant quantum compilation, this means sequence models can help with structure and resource estimation, but exact equivalence still needs verification, search, or stronger decoding strategies.
method: 44.8M-parameter encoder-decoder transformer with structured circuit tokenization
Tested on parameterized circuits (2–6 qubits) and Clifford+T circuits (3–6 qubits)
Compared hybrid post-processing, multi-candidate inference, and larger training sets
evidence_signal: On parameterized circuits, the hybrid pipeline reached median fidelity 1.000, while on Clifford+T circuits exact match fell from 88% for circuits with <=9 gates to near zero beyond 26 gates.
watch_item: Exact synthesis reliability degrades sharply with sequence length, so practical use requires equivalence checking and cannot rely on greedy autoregressive decoding alone.
paper_title: When Close Enough Is Not Enough: Autoregressive Drift in Quantum Circuit Synthesis
